title: Large network community detection by fast label propagation
method: Queue-based asynchronous label propagation revisits nodes affected by label changes, with a local maximal-support condition at normal termination.
datasets: Synthetic benchmark families and empirical networks, including Karate, Dolphins and Football.
metrics: Partition quality and runtime; local support guarantee.
locator: Algorithm 3; retention subsection; Results and empirical-network methods.
findings: The authors report substantial speed benefits over repeated full scans. Our study reproduces the core update rule, not their largest-scale numerical speed claims.
advantage: Simple queue bookkeeping reduces redundant visits.
limitation: Local label maximality does not guarantee useful or globally optimal communities.
relationship: Exact base method; already discusses retention, so retention is not an invented mechanism.

title: A community partitioning algorithm for cyberspace
authors: Kai Qi; Heng Zhang; Yang Zhou; Yifan Liu; Qingxiang Li
method: PR-LFM selects high-degree seeds, expands local-fitness communities, then uses PageRank to resolve overlapping assignments.
datasets: Classic social graphs and router-network examples; inspect the source-specific versions before reproduction.
findings: The paper reports competitive community division with a local-expansion pipeline. Its router experiments do not establish performance on our prepared benchmark versions.
advantage: Makes seed selection and overlap resolution explicit.
limitation: Resolution choices and router-data access complicate like-for-like reproduction.
relationship: A related local community method; our project keeps disjoint FLPA propagation rather than adopting PR-LFM.

title: Iterative embedding and reweighting of complex networks reveals community structure
authors: Bianka Kovács; Sadamori Kojaku; Gergely Palla; Santo Fortunato
method: Iterative embedding and reweighting alternates graph embeddings with geometry-derived edge-weight updates to separate communities.
datasets: Planted-partition and LFR synthetic networks, with additional network examples.
metrics: Element-centric similarity, NMI, detected community count and geometric separation.
locator: Results; Figures 3-6; Methods and supplementary sensitivity discussions.
findings: The authors show that reweighting can help conventional detectors recover planted structure. Weight interpretation depends on whether the embedding yields distances or proximities.
advantage: Separates a reusable graph transformation from downstream community detection.
limitation: Repeated embeddings cost more and introduce settings absent from our local feature rule.
relationship: Important reweighting prior art; our weights are computed once from local neighbourhood overlap.

title: GATFELPA integrates graph attention networks and enhanced label propagation for robust community detection
authors: Feiyi Tang; Junxian Li; Xi Liu; Chao Chang; Luyao Teng
method: GATFELPA combines graph attention, enhanced label propagation, adaptive aggregation depth and a similarity-preservation mechanism.
datasets: Cora, CiteSeer, PubMed and ogbn-arxiv attributed citation networks.
metrics: Community/clustering agreement, robustness and computational comparisons in the paper's own setup.
locator: Similarity preservation; Experimental analysis; ablation and parameter sections.
findings: The article reports favourable performance across its attributed-graph experiments. Those training and input conditions differ from topology-only FLPA.
advantage: Uses learned representations and local/global similarity information.
limitation: Model training, attributes and multiple components prevent a fair direct comparison without matching their protocol.
relationship: Shows that similarity-guided propagation is established; we do not claim to reproduce this neural model.

title: Graph embedding based label propagation for community detection in social networks
authors: Shyam Sundar Meena; Prakash Chandra Sharma; Yadvendra Pratap Singh; Mukund Pratap Singh
method: Embedding-based label propagation uses embedding similarities to weight neighbourhood label updates, mixing local connectivity with global representation.
datasets: Social-network benchmarks including Karate, Dolphins and Polbooks, plus LFR synthetic cases.
metrics: Modularity, community counts and partition-agreement measures reported in the article.
locator: Eq. 8; Algorithm 1; Tables 1-6 and LFR benchmark discussion.
findings: Reported tables compare the embedding-guided rule with other detectors. The paper's favourable findings are not a guarantee that our fixed local weighting will generalise.
advantage: Allows nonlocal structural information to influence propagation.
limitation: Embedding choices add a separate cost and selection budget; exact dataset/protocol alignment remains necessary.
relationship: A close similarity-weighted propagation relative, with embeddings replacing our fixed Jaccard feature.

title: Community detection in networks by dynamical optimal transport formulation
authors: Daniela Leite; Diego Baptista; Abdullahi A. Ibrahim; Enrico Facca; Caterina De Bacco
method: ORC-Nextrout uses dynamical optimal transport and Ollivier-Ricci geometry to control information flow between neighbourhoods.
datasets: SBM and LFR synthetic benchmarks and real networks with node metadata.
metrics: Adjusted Rand Index and comparisons across transport regimes.
locator: Results on community detection problems; Figures 3 and 5; Table 1.
findings: The authors show that transport settings change which structures can be recovered, with gains in parts of the tested regimes.
advantage: Provides a geometric interpretation of intra-community edges and bottlenecks.
limitation: Transport parameters and optimisation cost differ from lightweight propagation; best-setting results require attention to selection rules.
relationship: Motivates sensitivity to structural regimes and explicit parameter selection, not a direct implemented comparator.

title: Representative community divisions of networks
authors: Alec Kirkley; M. E. J. Newman
method: Clusters an ensemble of candidate network partitions into representative modes using an information-theoretic description of the solution set.
datasets: Synthetic and empirical partition ensembles generated for the same underlying networks.
metrics: Representativeness, partition description and diversity of competing community divisions.
locator: Results and discussion; Figure 1; mode-finding and partition-transmission formulation.
findings: The study explains why several plausible partitions can coexist and why a single optimum may hide important variation.
advantage: Treats variability as information to inspect rather than automatically as an error.
limitation: Requires an ensemble and answers a different question from producing a single propagation partition.
relationship: Supports our multi-seed analysis and caution that repeatability alone is not correctness.

title: Network community detection via neural embeddings
authors: Sadamori Kojaku; Filippo Radicchi; Yong-Yeol Ahn; Santo Fortunato
method: Analyses neural embeddings for community recovery, combining theoretical planted-model results with embedding and clustering experiments.
datasets: Planted-partition/SBM, LFR and empirical networks including Football.
metrics: Partition recovery and element-centric similarity across mixing and degree regimes.
locator: Figures 1-3; Simulations: LFR benchmark; theoretical assumptions in Methods.
findings: Certain shallow embedding methods can approach detectability limits under stated model assumptions, while sparse and unequal-community cases show important differences.
advantage: Connects practical representation methods to an explicit recovery framework.
limitation: Theoretical claims depend on model assumptions and do not certify arbitrary real networks or all embeddings.
relationship: Motivates varying synthetic between-community connectivity and keeping global-representation claims outside our local method.

title: Local dominance unveils clusters in networks
authors: Dingyi Shi; Fan Shang; Bingsheng Chen; Paul Expert; Linyuan Lü; H. Eugene Stanley; Renaud Lambiotte; Tim S. Evans; Ruiqi Li
method: Local Search derives community centres and hierarchies from local dominance relationships between nodes rather than iterative modularity optimisation.
datasets: Synthetic and empirical networks with reference labels, plus networks constructed from vector data.
metrics: Recovery quality, hierarchical structure, robustness and computational behaviour.
locator: Figures 1-3; Results; Methods and supplementary benchmark descriptions.
findings: The reported experiments show that local dominance captures structure that can differ from a modularity partition.
advantage: Uses a distinct local structural principle with interpretable centres.
limitation: Community-centre interpretation is a different objective, so matching modularity alone is insufficient for judging it.
relationship: Reinforces use of multiple metrics and the distinction between local structure and a global objective.

title: Betweenness-driven overlapping label propagation community detection
method: BD-LPA uses degree/betweenness-guided overlapping label propagation with pruning and refinement mechanisms.
datasets: Karate, Polbooks, Football and twelve LFR synthetic datasets.
metrics: Overlapping NMI, omega index, generalised F1, modularity and extended variation measures.
locator: Section 3; Tables 1-6; pruning and refinement descriptions.
findings: The authors report favourable overlapping-community results with configuration-dependent behaviour. This is a multi-membership problem, unlike our disjoint partitions.
advantage: Makes node importance and stability-related pruning explicit.
limitation: Overlapping metrics and tuning choices cannot be imported directly into a disjoint FLPA evaluation.
relationship: Recent propagation/stability prior art; demonstrates that importance weighting and pruning are established directions.
